walkthroughs.body_html: China hosts the world's largest internal migration: ~280 million floating population (NBS 2021) moving from rural inland provinces (Sichuan, Henan, Anhui) to coastal manufacturing hubs (Guangdong, Shanghai, Beijing). The hukou system, since 1958, restricts access to urban housing, schools and healthcare for unregistered migrants, producing a structurally segmented labour market. Reforms since 2014 ease hukou access in small cities but not megacities.

Global remittances to LMICs reached ~$669 billion in 2023 (World Bank), exceeding FDI in many states. Top recipients: India ($125bn), Mexico ($66bn), China ($50bn), Philippines ($40bn). Remittances stabilise consumption, reduce poverty, fund education, and finance small enterprise. Risks include: dependency, Dutch disease (currency appreciation hurting exports), and brain drain spillovers. The cost of sending remittances averages ~6%, above the SDG target of 3%.

Brain drain hits low-income origin countries: ~30% of doctors trained in sub-Saharan Africa work abroad; Malawi has 1.6 doctors per 10,000 people. However, brain gain via return migration, diaspora networks and remittances can offset losses. India's IT diaspora in Silicon Valley fostered Bangalore's tech boom from the 1990s. Bilateral agreements (e.g. UK NHS recruitment ethical code) attempt to manage flows but rarely halt them.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a refugee and an economic migrant?
options: Climate change only happens in summer.
A refugee is forced to flee due to persecution, war or disaster and has legal protections under international law; an economic migrant chooses to move primarily for work or better living standards.
Refugees come from war zones and economic migrants come from rich countries.
Refugees and economic migrants are basically the same thing.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a megacity and a world city?
options: Climate change only happens in summer.
Megacities and world cities are the same thing.
A megacity is defined by population (over 10 million); a world city is defined by global economic and cultural influence (e.g. New York, London) — so a city can be one without the other.
A megacity has over 1 million people and a world city has over 5 million.

mcqs.q: Why can a cold winter NOT disprove climate change?
options: Climate is the long-term statistical average; a single cold winter is a weather event. Climate change is the trend in averages and extremes over decades, not the absence of cold days.
Climate change only happens in summer.
Refugees come from war zones and economic migrants come from rich countries.
A really cold winter proves global warming is not happening.
